rationale: I read the complete held EO 11796 (39 FR 27891, signed July 30, 1974, Continuing the Regulation of Exports): issued under section 5(b) of the act of October 6, 1917 (12 U.S.C. 95a) because the Export Administration Act had expired, it continues EO 11533 and the export-control rules, regulations and actions in effect until amended or revoked. It has no own term. I read the held full text of EO 11798 (signed August 14, 1974), titled 'Revoking Executive Order No. 11796 of July 30, 1974, and Continuing in Effect Executive Order No. 11533': sec. 1 provides 'Executive Order No. 11796 of July 30, 1974, issued under the authority of the act of October 6, 1917, as amended (12 U.S.C. 95a), is hereby revoked, except that this revocation shall not affect any violation of any rules, regulations, orders, licenses, and other forms of administrative action under said order which occurred during the period said order was in effect.' That names EO 11796 by number and date and revokes the whole order. The savings exception preserves only liability for past violations, not the order's operation. Sec. 2 continues EO 11533 and the actions under it pursuant to Public Law 93-372, effective as of the close of July 30, 1974; that continuance rests on EO 11533 and the statute, not on EO 11796. D6 self-check: a search of the held full-run texts for '11796' finds only EO 11796 and EO 11798; no held later instrument names or restores EO 11796. The other dossier actor leads (EO 11810 of September 30, 1974 and EO 11940 of September 30, 1976, both continuing export regulation under section 5(b) of the 1917 act, and EO 11978 of 1977 on Southern Rhodesia trade) were read in the held texts; none names EO 11796. Later event on the revoking order: I read the held text of EO 12002 (signed July 7, 1977, Administration of the Export Administration Act of 1969, as amended; held as the APP transcription, no FR-original image held). Sec. 7 revokes EO 11533, EO 11683, EO 11798, EO 11818, EO 11907 and EO 11940. That revocation of EO 11798 does not revive EO 11796: EO 12002 neither names EO 11796 nor contains any revival wording, and the revocation of a revoking order does not by itself restore the order it revoked. Sec. 6 of EO 12002 keeps in force only the delegations, rules, regulations, orders, licenses and other administrative actions taken under, or continued in existence by, the revoked orders. Through EO 11798 sec. 2 that means EO 11533 and the actions under it, which EO 11798 continued under Public Law 93-372, not EO 11796; EO 11798 sec. 1 had already revoked EO 11796 outright. Sec. 6 also preserves past violations, as EO 11798 sec. 1 did. The 1977 revocation of EO 11798 therefore leaves the 1974 end of EO 11796 unchanged. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 11798, August 14, 1974' and the 1989 snapshot row (revoked, actor EO 11798) agree. Both history observations were reviewed. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing August 14, 1974) is not otherwise adjudicated.
